page: Google Cloud Platform t2a-standard-2 is an ARM-based general-purpose server instance powered by an Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor. It features 2 dedicated physical cores running at 3.0 GHz with one thread per core, providing a total of 2 vCPUs. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local NVMe storage or bundled GPUs, and it provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates that the t2a-standard-2 delivers average single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1812.29 and a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 24.01 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory-bound operations are limited. The multi-core stress-ng score of 3594.57 and Geekbench multi-core score of 1997.0 are categorized as weak and poor respectively. Memory bandwidth is a notable bottleneck, with uncached large-block read speeds at 26.99 GB/sec and write speeds at 16.42 GB/sec. Cryptographic performance is also low, as shown by a PassMark CPU encryption score of 321.71, though the processor does support hardware AES encryption.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, this instance offers a low-cost entry point into ARM64 development on Google Cloud, utilizing a power-efficient architecture that reduces resource overhead. The primary tradeoff is the lack of x86 instruction sets such as AVX, AVX-512, or AMX, alongside weak multi-threaded scaling and low memory bandwidth. It is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, ARM64 software compilation testing, basic text processing, and low-traffic web serving.
